primitives.name: Directed Overlap Metric
primitives.verbatim_quote: (1) in paper (paraphrased from text): S(T|B) = mean_i max_j |Spearman ρ(f_i^T, f_j^B)|, where f_i^T is the output vector of test feature i across the ~800 series, f_j^B likewise for benchmark feature j.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S(T|B)': 'dimensionless overlap score', 'f_i^T': 'output vector of test feature i across series', 'f_j^B': 'output vector of benchmark feature j across series', 'ρ': 'Spearman rank correlation coefficient'}
primitives.assumptions: Behavioral similarity = correlated outputs; diverse series set avoids spurious correlations; monotonic equivalence captured by Spearman ρ.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When |ρ| ≈ 0, indicating no behavioral overlap between feature sets.

layer2.mapping: Maps feature set redundancy to a probabilistic overlap measure in GSI's Bayesian inference framework, enabling model selection based on distinctiveness rather than internal implementation.
layer2.telemetry: Correlation-based behavioral similarity across 800 diverse time series.

primitives.name: Within-Set Redundancy via PCA
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Within-set redundancy:** PCA on the feature-output matrix per set; report number of PCs needed to capture 90% of variance (also proportion of variance in first few PCs).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'PC_k': 'k-th principal component', 'λ_i': 'eigenvalue of i-th component', 'n': 'total number of features'}
primitives.assumptions: Variance in PCA reflects information content; first few components capture dominant signal.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When k approaches n, indicating high redundancy or poor compression.

layer2.mapping: Reduces feature set dimensionality to identify core information sources, supporting GSE's kernel-based feature fusion strategies.
layer2.telemetry: Number of principal components required to explain 90% variance per feature set.

primitives.name: Timing Benchmark
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Timing:** median + IQR computation time per feature set across series lengths 100–1000.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'T': 'time-series length', 'Time_median(T)': 'median computation time', 'IQR(T)': 'interquartile range of computation times'}
primitives.assumptions: Synthetic white noise approximates typical workload; parallel execution on multi-core systems.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When computational cost exceeds acceptable latency thresholds for real-time processing.

layer2.mapping: Provides performance constraints for GSE's online feature extraction pipelines, informing trade-offs between feature richness and latency.
layer2.telemetry: Median computation time and interquartile range for feature sets across varying series lengths.

The directed overlap metric S(T|B) formalizes behavioral redundancy between feature sets by measuring Spearman correlation of their outputs across a diverse dataset. It enables practitioners to quantify how much new information a feature set T contributes beyond another set B. This is critical for GSI’s Bayesian model selection, where overlapping features increase epistemic uncertainty. The PCA-based redundancy measure complements this by identifying intrinsic dimensionality within each set, aiding GSE in optimizing feature fusion strategies. Timing benchmarks ensure that feature extraction remains viable for real-time applications. Together, these primitives form a triad of empirical rigor: behavioral distinctiveness, information efficiency, and computational feasibility. Failure modes include spurious correlations due to dataset bias, overfitting to specific series types, and outdated library versions affecting comparability.
